# The source's signed Stein energy is negative on actual mean columns

STATUS: ANALYTIC_PAPER_CANDIDATE awaiting independent review.
Base: 0fb70b28063e76b87e0ac0b5e2aab0019a74d604. Isolated research only.
Original full V/RH: OPEN. No negative original-V witness.

## S0. Bounded test, existing equation, and exact non-goal

The full-source differential equation and positive convolution forcing are
already in HYPERBOLIC_SOURCE_COMPENSATION L5. They are not newly discovered
source properties. Its scalar gauged Sturm energy was already excluded by
L9; its coupled field and subsequent renewal constructions are not reopened.
This test checks a DIFFERENT, specified reading: use L5 as a stationary
diffusion-minus-jump Stein identity and its quadratic energy on the actual
conditional-mean likelihood columns. No positivity premise is inserted.

The result below is a negative energy on admissible mean columns, whereas
the corresponding original one-node V is positive. Thus neither stationarity
nor the positive convolution forcing makes THIS energy a carrier of V.
It does not exclude a corrected full conditional field, which would have
to keep the original weight, mixed term and boundary. No new request to
construct a generic reservoir or source-support operator follows.

Accepted inputs, read and pinned separately:

- REPORT_2026-09-15_HYPERBOLIC_SOURCE_COMPENSATION.md, L1, L5, L18--L19.
- REPORT_2026-09-16_CONVOLUTION_RECIPROCITY_RIGIDITY.md, R2--R3 for m=4.

We use their previously accepted identities/tails, not a fresh audit of
the entire old ladder or its published probabilistic source. All new
calculations below use real integrals and exact differentiation only.

## S1. Fixed full source and the signed stationary identity

Let r=r_2 be the density of T=sum_(n>=1) Gamma(2,rate pi*n^2), and
r_4=r*r the density of T+T' for an independent copy. Every rate and mode
is retained. The exact identity L5 is

    6 r_4(t)=4t^2 r''(t)+(22t-4pi)r'(t)+20r(t), t>0.       (S1)

The full r is positive on (0,infinity), flat at zero, and its derivatives
decay exponentially at infinity, with polynomial factors. For a smooth
compactly supported test phi, integration by parts gives

    E phi(T+T')
      = E[(2/3)T^2 phi''(T)+(2pi/3-T)phi'(T)+phi(T)].      (S2)

Indeed the adjoint of 4t^2 d^2/dt^2 +(22t-4pi)d/dt +20,
acting on phi under dt, is 4t^2 phi''+(4pi-6t)phi'+6phi.
There are no hidden distributions or boundary terms for these tests.

Define on this initial test class

    (Jg)(t)=int_0^infinity [g(t+s)-g(t)]r(s)ds,
    (Ag)(t)=(2/3)t^2 g''(t)+(2pi/3-t)g'(t),
    Lg=Ag-Jg.                                            (S3)

Then E Lphi(T)=0. The sign preceding J is MINUS. This is a signed
stationary identity, not an assertion of a Markov generator or of a
contractive semigroup. In particular a positive jump rate may not be
substituted for this negative one while retaining S2.

## S2. The exact energy includes a negative jump term

For complex g in the above test class, direct product differentiation and
expansion of the jump yield

    L|g|^2-2 Re(conjugate(g)Lg)
       =(4/3)t^2 |g'(t)|^2
          -int_0^infinity |g(t+s)-g(t)|^2 r(s)ds.

Using S2 for |g|^2 therefore gives the exact energy

    D[g]:=-2 Re int_0^infinity conjugate(g)Lg r dt
         =(4/3)int_0^infinity t^2 |g'|^2 r dt
             -E|g(T+T')-g(T)|^2.                        (S4)

This is the full signed expression. The two expectations are not made
independent when they share T. Stationarity alone gives the equality in
S4, not D>=0. We next test D on actual source mean columns, rather than
on an unrelated arbitrary probability law.

## S3. Actual mean likelihoods and admissibility

For 1/2<a<1 let x=(log a)/2 in I=(-log(2)/2,0), and put

    g_a(t)=a^(5/4) r(at)/r(t).                            (S5)

This is exactly Cg_x=E_(p_t)g_x in the original conditional-field source
report L18--L19. It is not a newly chosen exponential surrogate.
The measure in S4 is r(t)dt, deliberately distinguished from the physical
measure eta with its t>=1 cutoff and outer theta weight.

For the following limit restrict a to (1/2,3/4], and set

    sigma_a=pi(1-a), d_a=pi-2sigma_a=pi(2a-1)>0.

The full theta series and its derivatives give, uniformly in this a range,
as t tends to infinity,

    r(t)=4pi^2 t exp(-pi t)[1+O(1/t)],
    g_a(t)=a^(9/4) exp(sigma_a t)[1+O(1/t)],
    g_a'(t)=a^(9/4) exp(sigma_a t)[sigma_a+O(1/t)].         (S6)

For clarity the full leading formula is
r(t)=4pi^2 t exp(-pi t)[1-3/(2pi t)+O(exp(-3pi t))].
Its differentiated series gives the corresponding logarithmic derivative.
Applying it at at>=t/2 proves uniformity in S6; r is bounded below by
its positive leading expression for sufficiently large t. No finite-mode
substitution for the source is made.

At zero, exact reciprocity r(1/t)=t^(5/2)r(t) gives

    r(t)=4pi^2 t^(-7/2) exp(-pi/t)[1+O(t)],
    g_a(t)=a^(-9/4) exp[-pi(1/a-1)/t][1+O(t)].             (S7)

The differentiated estimates hold too. Since 1/a-1>=1/3 in the chosen
range, g_a and its first two derivatives are uniformly bounded near zero
by fixed powers of 1/t times exp(-pi/(3t)). On every intermediate compact,
uniform bounds follow from smoothness and the positive r denominator.
In particular g_a(t)<=C exp(sigma_a t) for all t>0, uniformly in this range.

For each fixed a>1/2 all terms in S4 are finite. For example the square
at T+T' is integrable against r_4, and all derivative terms against r,
because their exponent at infinity is -d_a t with polynomial factors.
All origin products vanish by S7. Thus S2 extends to |g_a|^2 directly
by integration by parts with its paid endpoints; Fubini for the jump is
absolute. This proves S4 for the actual g_a, not merely for compact tests.

## S4. Leading full-energy comparison at the admissible endpoint

From S6 and the elementary integral int_0^infinity t^3 exp(-d t)dt=6/d^4,

    lim_(a down to 1/2) [d_a^4/a^(9/2)]
        (4/3)int_0^infinity t^2 |g_a'|^2 r dt = 8pi^4.    (S8)

Indeed the leading integrand is (16/3)pi^2 a^(9/2) sigma_a^2
t^3 exp(-d_a t). Its integral, after scaling, is
32pi^2 sigma_a^2 ->8pi^4. The uniform O(1/t) errors in S6 contribute
O(d_a^(-3)) before scaling; a fixed initial interval is uniformly bounded.
These statements can also be checked after the substitution v=d_a t.

The accepted full convolution tail for m=4 is

    r_4(t)=(8pi^4/3)t^3 exp(-pi t)[1+O(1/t)].             (S9)

It follows from the complete convolution source, not a replacement by a
single shape-four gamma. Therefore S6 and S9 imply

    lim_(a down to 1/2) [d_a^4/a^(9/2)] E[g_a(T+T')^2]
       =16pi^4.                                         (S10)

The other two terms in the expansion of the squared jump have smaller
order. With M(theta)=E exp(theta T), the full source tail implies
M(2sigma_a)=O(d_a^(-2)), while M(sigma_a)<=M(pi/2)<infinity.
The global bound following S7 gives

    E g_a(T)^2 <= C^2 M(2sigma_a)=O(d_a^(-2)),
    E[g_a(T+T')g_a(T)]
       <=C^2 M(2sigma_a)M(sigma_a)=O(d_a^(-2)).            (S11)

Independence is used only for T and T' in this upper bound; the shared T
is counted twice in its exponential. Both S11 terms vanish after the
scaling in S10. Combining the complete S4, S8, S10 and S11 proves

    lim_(a down to 1/2) [d_a^4/a^(9/2)] D[g_a] = -8pi^4 <0.  (S12)

Consequently D[g_a]<0 for every sufficiently small positive a-1/2.
All such a remain strictly inside the original admissible interval.
No numerical node, quadrature or finite theta scan is used. The boundary
a=1/2 is used only as a limit; divergent endpoint energies are not tests.

## S5. Original V on these same one-node signals has the opposite sign

For the ORIGINAL f=Phi/||Phi||_2, evenness and the full decay give directly

    V(x,x)=2int_x^infinity u f(u)^2 du
          =2int_|x|^infinity u f(u)^2 du>0.                (S13)

This holds for every real x, including x=(log a)/2 above. Thus D[g_a]
cannot equal V(x,x), nor a positive constant multiple or positive
node-weighted version of it, on the whole required class. A stationary
identity with the exact source and its square-rate coefficient is not
by itself an original-V nonnegative energy representation.

Scope: the failure is precisely the unweighted diffusion-minus-additive-
jump energy S4 on the actual conditional MEANS S5. It is not a sign
claim for the full conditional-field energy with physical eta, for any
of its cutoff boundary corrections, or for another coupled operator.
S1 is inherited old mathematics; S2--S12 are the bounded energy test.
No new source-sign supplier, canonical admission, or counter reset.

# Independent review: the unweighted signed Stein energy

**Verdict: ACCEPT_ACTUAL_MEAN_SIGNED_STEIN_ENERGY_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.**

The complete `HYPERBOLIC_STEIN_ENERGY_CANDIDATE.md` was read and independently checked, bound to SHA256 `7955245e345793cc6a82e4e4ef84eaf4627a3c9ea2153544631e3c4e2ae7eafd` (8858 bytes). S0–S5 pass. In particular the limit of d_a^4 D[g_a]/a^(9/2) is exactly -8 pi^4. No correction is required for the stated scope.

This is an analytic obstruction for the particular unweighted diffusion-minus-additive-jump energy on the actual conditional-mean columns. It does not give a negative original V, a failure of the full conditional energy with its physical weight and boundary, or an RH conclusion.

## 1. Exact pins, source use and prior scope

The complete adjacent manifest `HYPERBOLIC_STEIN_ENERGY_PINS.json` has SHA256 `3852679231df8f4da650967ce24ceafe0035f2d581664d2cddc8fa021990396c`. Every listed local input hash was checked in the isolated `gamma-reciprocity-worktree`:

- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-15_HYPERBOLIC_SOURCE_COMPENSATION.md`: `feeb23e50223e5d85b16b8f6f1e83f849a9029f6f9aa8d4f47ad70cd4f5dad21` (17381 bytes), read completely. The needed identities are L1, formula L5, and L18–L19; L9 was also checked for the distinction from its earlier gauged-energy obstruction.
- `docs/Codex/REPORT_2026-09-16_CONVOLUTION_RECIPROCITY_RIGIDITY.md`: `52fecee7e98bf9fa1fbd00a90ec4b606c7cc2a8688fc5d327a53f4d179dbd535` (8220 bytes), read completely. R2–R3 provide the complete convolution tail with shape m=4.
- `orchestrator/state/CHANNEL_RUNTIME.json`: `f7bb8eed28bf9b67292f67bbbdde96cecb4baf42e758e0acbb4be34d5baa6418`. Its hash is a source-manifest check, not a mathematical hypothesis or permission for a new native effect.

Earlier source identities and their recorded acceptance are inherited, not advertised as newly independently audited in their entirety. No new external theorem is needed for S1–S12: the new argument uses differentiation, integration by parts, the full tails, product expansion and elementary integrals. It does not reimport the old probabilistic primary theorem as a positivity theorem for this operator.

The fixed source equation, its Riccati/gauge interpretations, and the scalar gauge obstruction are old material. Here the test is specifically its adjoint stationary identity on r(t)dt and the associated signed quadratic expression on Cg_x. That is distinct from L9, which uses a gauged differential operator on the log-coordinate half-line and a particular source function with a Neumann endpoint. The difference is stated without claiming a new source property, reopening the old ladder, or certifying literature novelty.

## 2. S1: adjoint coefficients and the necessary minus sign

For the source identity

    6r_4 = 4t^2 r'' +(22t-4pi)r' +20r,

the formal adjoint on the test phi with respect to dt is

    (4t^2 phi)'' -((22t-4pi)phi)' +20phi
      =4t^2 phi'' +(4pi-6t)phi' +6phi.

Thus division by 6 gives exactly S2. On initial compact smooth tests all boundary terms vanish; the source is smooth and flat at zero and decays with its derivatives at infinity. The identity involves the density r*r of two independent full copies, so E phi(T+T') is exactly its left side.

With A=(2/3)t^2 partial_t^2 +(2pi/3-t)partial_t, S2 says

    E Aphi(T)=E phi(T+T')-E phi(T)=E Jphi(T).

Consequently the stationary operator is L=A-J. Replacing it by A+J would not preserve this identity. A negative jump coefficient is not a Markov jump generator with positive rates, and no contractivity conclusion follows from the word stationary. The candidate makes this distinction correctly.

## 3. S2: full energy and shared-variable structure

For complex g, the drift terms cancel in the product rule and the diffusion part gives (4/3)t^2 |g'|^2. At fixed t the jump product identity is

    J|g|^2 -2 Re(conjugate(g)Jg)
      = integral |g(t+s)-g(t)|^2 r(s)ds.

Since L contains -J, this term enters with the negative sign in S4. Integrating the complete identity and using E L|g|^2=0 yields exactly

    -2 Re E[conjugate(g(T)) Lg(T)]
      =(4/3)E[T^2|g'(T)|^2]-E|g(T+T')-g(T)|^2.

The second expectation has a common T in both terms of the difference. It is not the difference of evaluations at two independent arguments. The initial compact smooth class justifies this calculation, and the extension for the growing g_a is checked below rather than presumed.

## 4. S3: exact mean column and admissible limiting regime

The source report has p_t(s)=t h(ts)h(t(1-s))/r(t) and

    g_x(t,s)=a^(9/4) h(ats)h(at(1-s))/(h(ts)h(t(1-s))).

Integration over s in (0,1), followed by the convolution change of variables, gives

    E_(p_t)g_x=a^(9/4) t/r(t) * r(at)/(at)
              =a^(5/4)r(at)/r(t)=g_a(t).

Thus the column is literal, with the full h and r, not an exponential replacement. The relation a=exp(2x) sends a in (1/2,1) exactly into the original I=(-log(2)/2,0). The limit a decreasing to 1/2 stays strictly inside I until the endpoint, which is not used as an admissible finite-energy test.

The energy uses r(t)dt on the whole positive axis. The physical measure in old L18 is instead supported on t>=1 and has the extra t^(3/2)r(t)^2 p_t(s)/(2||Phi||_2^2) factor. This distinction is material and is correctly retained.

## 5. Uniform full-source estimates and extension beyond compact tests

The complete large-t series has leading expression

    r(t)=4pi^2 t exp(-pi t) [1-3/(2pi t)+epsilon(t)].

The n>=2 terms, including each fixed differentiated series, are bounded by constants times exp(-3pi t) relative to this leading factor for t large. The polynomial powers of n from differentiation remain summable against the exponential gap. In particular epsilon and its first required derivatives have such bounds. The positive leading bracket is bounded away from zero for sufficiently large t.

Uniformly for a in (1/2,3/4], both t and at are in this regime when t is sufficiently large independently of a. Taking the ratio gives the factor a^(9/4) and exp(pi(1-a)t), with relative error O(1/t). Differentiating the actual ratio, rather than an unspecified remainder, gives

    g_a'/g_a = a r'(at)/r(at)-r'(t)/r(t)
              =pi(1-a)+O(t^-2).

Here the 1/t terms in the two logarithmic derivatives cancel. This is stronger than the uniform derivative estimate S6 needs. The same differentiated full-series bounds control the second derivative by a fixed polynomial times exp(sigma_a t).

At zero, reciprocity yields r(t)=t^(-5/2)r(1/t), hence the t^(-7/2) leading power and exp(-pi/t). Substitution into the exact ratio gives the factor a^(-9/4) and exp[-pi(1/a-1)/t] in S7. For this a range, 1/a-1>=1/3. Differentiation introduces only fixed inverse powers of t and constants uniformly bounded in a. Thus g_a and its first two derivatives are uniformly controlled near zero by exp(-pi/(3t)) times fixed powers of 1/t. Intermediate compact intervals are uniformly bounded by smoothness, positivity of r, and the compact parameter interval [1/2,3/4]. This also proves the asserted global bound g_a(t)<=C exp(sigma_a t) with one constant C.

For fixed a>1/2, d_a=pi(2a-1)>0. At infinity, every integration-by-parts boundary product for phi=g_a^2 consists of a polynomial times exp(-d_a t), and so tends to zero. At zero the reciprocal tails make all these products vanish. All required r-weighted derivatives are integrable. The r_4-weighted square is integrable by its t^3 exp(-pi t) tail. Finally the mixed jump integral is absolutely convergent: the same global bound gives finite M(2sigma_a)M(sigma_a). Thus S2 extends directly to g_a^2 and S4 to g_a. There is no unpaid compact-support removal or unhandled endpoint distribution. Uniform integrability at the limiting a=1/2 is neither true nor assumed.

## 6. S4: exact leading constants and lower-order terms

For the diffusion term, the uniform estimates give the leading integrand

    (16/3)pi^2 a^(9/2) sigma_a^2 t^3 exp(-d_a t).

Its integral is 32pi^2 a^(9/2) sigma_a^2/d_a^4. The relative O(1/t) error is bounded in absolute value by a constant times t^2 exp(-d_a t), whose integral is O(d_a^-3). A fixed initial interval contributes a uniformly bounded quantity. Since a stays bounded away from zero and sigma_a tends to pi/2,

    (d_a^4/a^(9/2)) * diffusion term -> 8pi^4.

The complete-source R3 with m=4 has coefficient (2pi)^4/Gamma(4)=8pi^4/3, so S9 is exact at the needed order. This coefficient includes the full higher-rate tail; it is not the coefficient of a standalone shape-four, rate-pi gamma law. Multiplying by g_a^2 gives the leading integrand

    (8pi^4/3) a^(9/2) t^3 exp(-d_a t).

Again the uniform error is O(t^2 exp(-d_a t)) and the initial interval is uniformly bounded. Therefore the scaled E g_a(T+T')^2 tends to 16pi^4. In both calculations the elementary integral is 6/d_a^4. No exchange of a divergent endpoint integral with a limit is used.

The remaining expansion terms really have smaller order. The full r tail implies M(2sigma_a)=O(d_a^-2), and sigma_a<=pi/2 gives M(sigma_a)<=M(pi/2)<infinity. The bounds are uniform for a approaching 1/2 from above. In particular

    E[g_a(T+T')g_a(T)]
       <=C^2 E exp(sigma_a(2T+T'))
       = C^2 M(2sigma_a)M(sigma_a)=O(d_a^-2).

Independence is used only between T and T'; the coefficient 2 on the shared T is indispensable and is present. Also E g_a(T)^2=O(d_a^-2). Expanding the jump square as E g_a(T+T')^2 -2E[g_a(T+T')g_a(T)]+E g_a(T)^2 therefore gives scaled limit 16pi^4, not a sum of fictitiously independent variances.

Subtracting this jump term from the diffusion term establishes

    lim_(a down to 1/2) d_a^4 D[g_a]/a^(9/2)=-8pi^4.

Since the scaling factor is positive and finite for each admissible a, D[g_a]<0 for every a sufficiently close to 1/2 from above. An explicit first a or quantitative threshold is not asserted or needed. Each test has finite energy; only the normalized asymptotic uses the inadmissible endpoint as a limit.

## 7. S5: original diagonal and exclusion scope

For the original positive even f, shifting u=X+x gives V(x,x)=2 integral_x^infinity u f(u)^2 du. If x<0, the integral over [x,-x] vanishes because the integrand is odd. This leaves the positive tail starting at |x|; x>=0 gives the same formula directly. Thus V(x,x)>0 for the actual nodes just used, and indeed for every real x.

A negative D[g_a] on an admissible one-node mean cannot equal that original diagonal, any positive constant multiple, or a positive node weight times it. This also disproves nonnegativity of the specified energy on the claimed whole class, since one actual mean column already fails. It does not establish that some alternative sign convention or additional correction is a valid positive representation; those are separate constructions.

The scope is exactly S4 on the conditional means under the unweighted probability measure r(t)dt. It does not settle the full conditional-field energy, physical eta, mixed coefficient terms, the t=1 cutoff or its boundary corrections, a different coupled operator, original all-row V, or RH. The inherited source equation is not new sign progress. The bounded result rejects the specified stationary signed energy as a positive realization and leaves those other questions open.

Only this assigned private review file was written. Foreign canonical observation-only HOLD and all other files were preserved. No descendants, canonical mutation, new hunt, numerical source evaluation, Lean run, external dispatch, commit or publication were performed.

Verdict: ACCEPT_ACTUAL_MEAN_SIGNED_STEIN_ENERGY_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
The complete independent review was read; no correction was requested.
Review SHA256: d88e537108cb4ba61e9b435a3db946d2a115f7ad585e7d77c846f68accb6c40d.
Candidate SHA256: 7955245e345793cc6a82e4e4ef84eaf4627a3c9ea2153544631e3c4e2ae7eafd.
Base: 0fb70b28063e76b87e0ac0b5e2aab0019a74d604.

The full candidate was read, alongside the precise L1/L5/L18/L19 source
identities and R2/R3 convolution tail. The old source equation, old negative
gauged Sturm test and old coupled ladder remain old results. This checks one
different specified quadratic expression; no positive route is opened by it.

1. Adjoint and product signs. For the density operator in S1 the test
   adjoint is (4t^2 phi)''-((22t-4pi)phi)'+20phi. Its phi' coefficient
   is 16t-22t+4pi=4pi-6t; its phi coefficient is 8-22+20=6.
   Thus E(Aphi)=E(phi(T+T')-phi(T)) and L=A-J, not A+J.
   The diffusion product defect is (4/3)t^2|g'|^2. The jump product
   defect is E_s|g(t+s)-g(t)|^2 and enters with a minus sign. Integration
   against the invariant density gives precisely S4 with the stated sign.

2. The mean column is the actual source column. Integrating the conditional
   likelihood against p_t cancels the two h denominators and changes
   variables u=ats. The remaining integral is r(at)/(at). Multiplying by
   a^(9/4)t/r(t) gives a^(5/4)r(at)/r(t). This is g_a; its t measure in
   S4 remains r(t)dt, not eta. Admissibility is a>1/2, or x>-log(2)/2.

3. Uniformity and endpoints. At infinity r(t) has leading coefficient
   4pi^2 t; hence the ratio in S5 has amplitude a^(9/4), not a^(5/4).
   At zero reciprocity gives t^(-7/2) exp(-pi/t) and the ratio has
   amplitude a^(-9/4). Uniform derivative estimates follow by differentiating
   the full convergent theta series at t and at>=t/2. On a in [1/2,3/4],
   near zero every fixed derivative is bounded by a power of 1/t times
   exp(-pi/(3t)); intermediate compact intervals use r>0. At infinity
   g_a and its first two derivatives are bounded by C exp(sigma_a t).
   For each fixed admissible a, r times |g_a|^2 and its derivatives has
   exponent -d_a t. The IBP boundary products t^2 r'|g_a|^2,
   t^2 r (|g_a|^2)' and (22t-4pi)r|g_a|^2 vanish at both ends.
   Absolute integrability also holds for g_a Ag_a, r_4 g_a^2 and the jump
   cross term below. Thus the stationary identity can be used without
   inserting an invalid infinite-energy endpoint test.

4. Independent leading-order arithmetic. In R3 for m=4 the full tail
   amplitude is (2pi)^4/Gamma(4)=8pi^4/3. For the diffusion integral the
   amplitude of t^3 exp(-d_a t) is (16/3)pi^2 a^(9/2) sigma_a^2;
   multiplication by 6/d_a^4 yields scaled limit 8pi^4. For E g_a(T+T')^2
   it yields 16pi^4. Uniform relative O(1/t) errors integrate to O(d_a^-3)
   and vanish after d_a^4 scaling. The fixed initial interval is uniformly
   bounded; the estimates do not take an unproved global dominated limit.

5. Entire jump and shared variables. Expanding the jump square gives
   E g_a(T+T')^2 - 2 E[g_a(T+T')g_a(T)] + E g_a(T)^2.
   The global exponential upper bound gives a cross bound
   C^2 M(2sigma_a)M(sigma_a), not C^2 M(sigma_a)^3. Here T occurs twice,
   T' once. The first factor is O(d_a^-2), and the second is uniformly
   finite as sigma_a<=pi/2. The standalone square is also O(d_a^-2).
   Both vanish after scaling; no cancellation was silently omitted.
   Thus the complete scaled energy tends to -8pi^4.

6. Scope. The same node has original V(x,x)>0 by evenness. Therefore S4
   is not original V or a positive rescaling of it on the mean-column class.
   This does not evaluate any compensated energy with physical eta, nor
   produce a negative original-V witness. It excludes this attempted
   source-stationary energy interpretation only. No Lean claim, source-sign
